title: C Programming Mastery
subtitle: Complete Guide from Beginner to Advanced
author: Systems Programming Experts

chapters.title: Introduction to C
chapters.description: Understanding the basics of C programming language

pages.title: What is C Programming
pages.content: C is a general-purpose procedural programming language developed by Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs in 1972. It is widely used for system programming, operating systems, embedded systems, and performance-critical applications. C provides low-level memory access through pointers and is considered the foundation for many modern programming languages such as C++, Java, and Python.
keyPoints: C is a procedural programming language
Used in operating systems and embedded systems
Provides direct memory access using pointers

quiz.question: Who developed the C programming language?
quiz.explanation: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in 1972.

pages.title: Structure of a C Program
pages.content: A C program consists of several components including header files, the main() function, variable declarations, statements, and return statements. Every C program execution begins from the main() function.
keyPoints: Every C program starts execution from main()
Statements inside main() define program logic

quiz.question: Which function is the entry point of a C program?
quiz.explanation: Execution of every C program starts from the main() function.

pages.title: Compilation Process
pages.content: A C program goes through several stages before becoming an executable file. The stages include preprocessing, compilation, assembling, and linking.
pages.exampleCode: gcc program.c -o program
keyPoints: Compiler converts code into assembly language
Assembler converts assembly to machine code

quiz.question: Which step creates the final executable file?
quiz.explanation: The linker combines object files and libraries to create the executable.

chapters.title: Variables & Data Types
chapters.description: Understanding variables, data types, and memory usage in C

pages.title: Variables in C
pages.content: A variable in C is a named storage location used to store data. Every variable has a data type that defines what type of data it can hold. Variables must be declared before they are used in a program. The declaration tells the compiler the variable's name and the type of value it will store.
keyPoints: Each variable has a specific data type
Variables must be declared before use

quiz.question: What is a variable in C?
quiz.explanation: A variable is a named memory location used to store data.

pages.title: Basic Data Types
pages.content: Data types define the type of data a variable can store. C provides several basic data types such as int, char, float, and double. Each data type occupies a specific amount of memory and is used for different types of values.

quiz.question: Which data type stores decimal values?
quiz.explanation: float and double are used for decimal numbers.

pages.title: Size of Data Types
pages.content: Each data type in C occupies a specific amount of memory. The size may vary depending on the compiler and system architecture, but commonly used sizes are int (4 bytes), char (1 byte), float (4 bytes), and double (8 bytes).
keyPoints: Different data types use different memory
Efficient memory usage is important in C

quiz.question: Which operator is used to find the size of a data type?
quiz.explanation: sizeof operator returns the memory size of a variable or data type.

pages.title: Type Modifiers
pages.content: Type modifiers are used to modify the size or range of basic data types. Common modifiers include short, long, signed, and unsigned. They allow programmers to optimize memory usage and define variable ranges.

quiz.question: Which modifier allows only positive values?
quiz.explanation: unsigned data types store only positive values.

chapters.title: Operators in C
chapters.description: Understanding different types of operators used in C programming

pages.title: Arithmetic Operators
pages.content: Arithmetic operators are used to perform mathematical operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and modulus. These operators work with numeric data types such as int, float, and double.

quiz.question: Which operator returns the remainder of a division?
quiz.explanation: The modulus (%) operator returns the remainder after division.

pages.title: Relational Operators
pages.content: Relational operators are used to compare two values. The result of a relational operation is either true (1) or false (0). These operators are commonly used in decision-making statements such as if and while.

quiz.question: Which operator checks if two values are equal?
quiz.explanation: == is used to check equality between two values.

pages.title: Logical Operators
pages.content: Logical operators are used to combine multiple conditions in a program. They are mostly used in conditional statements such as if and loops.

quiz.question: Which operator represents logical AND?
quiz.explanation: && is the logical AND operator.

pages.title: Assignment Operators
pages.content: Assignment operators are used to assign values to variables. The basic assignment operator is '='. There are also compound assignment operators that combine arithmetic operations with assignment.

quiz.question: Which operator adds a value and assigns it to a variable?
quiz.explanation: += adds the value and assigns the result.

pages.title: Increment and Decrement Operators
pages.content: Increment and decrement operators are used to increase or decrease the value of a variable by 1. They are commonly used in loops and counters.

quiz.question: Which operator increases a value by 1?
quiz.explanation: ++ is the increment operator.

chapters.title: Control Statements
chapters.description: Decision-making statements used to control the flow of a program

pages.title: if Statement
pages.content: The if statement is used to execute a block of code only when a specified condition is true. It allows programs to make decisions based on conditions.
keyPoints: Executes code only if condition is true

quiz.question: Which statement is used for decision making?
quiz.explanation: The if statement executes code when a condition is true.

pages.title: if-else Statement
pages.content: The if-else statement is used when two possible outcomes exist. If the condition is true, the if block executes. Otherwise, the else block executes.
keyPoints: if block runs when condition is true
else block runs when condition is false

quiz.question: Which block runs when the condition is false?
quiz.explanation: The else block executes when the if condition is false.

pages.title: switch Statement
pages.content: The switch statement allows a variable to be tested against multiple values. It is often used instead of multiple if-else statements for better readability.
keyPoints: default runs when no case matches

quiz.question: Which keyword prevents fall-through in switch?
quiz.explanation: break stops execution of further cases.

chapters.title: Loops
chapters.description: Repetition statements used to execute code multiple times

pages.title: for Loop
pages.content: The for loop is used when the number of iterations is known. It consists of initialization, condition, and increment/decrement.
keyPoints: Used when number of iterations is known

quiz.question: Which loop is commonly used when the number of iterations is known?
quiz.explanation: The for loop is ideal when the iteration count is known.

pages.title: while Loop
pages.content: The while loop repeatedly executes a block of code as long as the condition remains true.
keyPoints: Loop runs while condition is true
Useful when iteration count is unknown

quiz.question: When is the condition checked in a while loop?
quiz.explanation: The while loop checks the condition before executing the loop body.

pages.title: do-while Loop
pages.content: The do-while loop executes the block of code at least once before checking the condition.

quiz.question: Which loop executes at least once?
quiz.explanation: The do-while loop executes the body before checking the condition.

chapters.title: Functions
chapters.description: Reusable blocks of code used to perform specific tasks

pages.title: Introduction to Functions
pages.content: A function in C is a block of code that performs a specific task. Functions help organize programs into smaller modules, making code easier to read, reuse, and maintain. Every C program contains at least one function, which is the main() function.
keyPoints: main() is the entry point of a C program

quiz.question: Which function is the entry point of a C program?
quiz.explanation: Execution of every C program starts from the main() function.

pages.title: Function Declaration and Definition
pages.content: In C, functions are usually declared before they are used. The declaration tells the compiler the function's name, return type, and parameters. The definition contains the actual code that runs when the function is called.
keyPoints: Declaration informs compiler about the function

quiz.question: What does a function declaration specify?
quiz.explanation: Function declaration specifies the name, return type, and parameters.

pages.title: Function Parameters
pages.content: Functions can accept input values called parameters. These values are passed when the function is called. Parameters allow functions to work with different values each time they run.
keyPoints: Parameters allow passing values to functions
Values are passed during function call

quiz.question: What are inputs passed to functions called?
quiz.explanation: Parameters are values passed into functions.

pages.title: Return Values
pages.content: Functions can return values to the calling function using the return keyword. The return type of the function must match the type of value returned.
keyPoints: Return type must match function declaration
Functions can return only one value

quiz.question: Which keyword is used to return a value from a function?
quiz.explanation: The return keyword returns a value from a function.

pages.title: Recursion
pages.content: Recursion is a technique where a function calls itself to solve a problem. Recursive functions must have a base condition to stop infinite recursion.

quiz.question: What is recursion?
quiz.explanation: Recursion occurs when a function calls itself.

chapters.title: Arrays
chapters.description: Understanding arrays and how to store multiple values in a single variable

pages.title: Introduction to Arrays
pages.content: An array is a collection of elements of the same data type stored in contiguous memory locations. Arrays allow programmers to store multiple values using a single variable name. Each value in an array is accessed using an index number. In C programming, array indexing starts from 0.
keyPoints: Array stores multiple values of the same type
Elements are stored in contiguous memory
Array size must be specified during declaration

quiz.question: What is the starting index of an array in C?
quiz.explanation: Array indexing in C starts from 0.

pages.title: Array Declaration and Initialization
pages.content: Arrays must be declared before they are used. The declaration includes the data type, array name, and the number of elements it can store. Arrays can also be initialized at the time of declaration.
keyPoints: Array must be declared before use
Elements are accessed using index numbers
Initialization can be done during declaration

quiz.question: Which syntax correctly declares an array?
quiz.explanation: int arr[5]; declares an array with 5 elements.

pages.title: Using Loops with Arrays
pages.content: Loops are commonly used with arrays to access each element. Instead of manually printing each value, loops allow programmers to iterate through array elements efficiently.
keyPoints: Commonly used loop is the for loop

quiz.question: Which loop is commonly used to traverse arrays?
quiz.explanation: The for loop is commonly used to iterate through arrays.

pages.title: Multidimensional Arrays
pages.content: Multidimensional arrays are arrays of arrays. They are commonly used to represent tables or matrices. The most common type is a two-dimensional array.

quiz.question: How many indices are required for a 2D array?
quiz.explanation: Two-dimensional arrays require two indices.

pages.title: Array Program Example
pages.content: Arrays are often used in programs where multiple values must be processed together. For example, calculating the sum of elements in an array.
keyPoints: Used with loops for processing elements
Common operations include sum, average, search

quiz.question: Which variable stores the result in the example program?
quiz.explanation: The variable sum stores the total of array elements.

chapters.title: Strings
chapters.description: Understanding strings and string manipulation in C programming

pages.title: Introduction to Strings
pages.content: A string in C is a sequence of characters terminated by a null character '\0'. Strings are stored in character arrays. Unlike some modern languages, C does not have a built-in string data type, so strings are handled using arrays of characters.
keyPoints: Strings are stored in character arrays
Strings end with a null character '\0'
Strings are printed using %s format specifier

quiz.question: Which character terminates a string in C?
quiz.explanation: Strings in C end with a null character '\0'.

pages.title: String Input and Output
pages.content: Strings can be read and displayed using functions such as scanf() and gets(). The printf() function is used to display strings. However, scanf() stops reading input when it encounters a space.
keyPoints: Arrays must have enough memory to store characters

quiz.question: Which format specifier is used to print a string?
quiz.explanation: %s is used to print strings.

pages.title: String Functions
pages.content: C provides several built-in string handling functions in the string.h library. These functions help perform operations such as finding string length, copying strings, comparing strings, and concatenating strings.
keyPoints: strcpy() copies one string to another

quiz.question: Which function returns the length of a string?
quiz.explanation: strlen() calculates the number of characters in a string.

pages.title: String Comparison
pages.content: The strcmp() function compares two strings. It returns 0 if the strings are equal, a positive value if the first string is greater, and a negative value if the second string is greater.

quiz.question: What does strcmp() return if two strings are equal?
quiz.explanation: strcmp returns 0 when both strings are equal.

pages.content: Strings are commonly used in real-world programs such as storing names, sentences, and text data. Below is a simple program that calculates the length of a string manually.
keyPoints: Strings are processed character by character
Loops are used for string traversal

quiz.question: Which character indicates the end of a string?
quiz.explanation: The null character '\0' marks the end of a string.

chapters.title: Pointers
chapters.description: Understanding memory addresses and pointer variables in C

pages.title: Introduction to Pointers
pages.content: A pointer is a variable that stores the memory address of another variable. Instead of storing a value directly, a pointer stores the location of the value in memory. Pointers are powerful features of the C language and are used for dynamic memory allocation, arrays, and function arguments.

quiz.question: What does a pointer store?
quiz.explanation: Pointers store the memory address of a variable.

pages.title: Address Operator (&)
pages.content: The address-of operator (&) is used to obtain the memory address of a variable. This address can then be stored in a pointer variable.

quiz.question: Which operator returns the memory address of a variable?
quiz.explanation: & operator returns the address of a variable.

pages.title: Dereference Operator (*)
pages.content: The dereference operator (*) is used to access the value stored at the memory address pointed to by a pointer. It allows programmers to manipulate the actual data stored in memory.
keyPoints: * accesses the value at the address

quiz.question: What does *ptr represent?
quiz.explanation: *ptr accesses the value stored at the memory location.

pages.title: Pointer Arithmetic
pages.content: Pointer arithmetic allows pointers to move through memory locations. It is commonly used when working with arrays.
keyPoints: Pointer increments move to next memory location

quiz.question: What does ptr + 1 represent?
quiz.explanation: ptr + 1 moves the pointer to the next memory location.

pages.title: Pointers with Arrays
pages.content: Pointers and arrays are closely related in C. The name of an array itself represents the address of the first element.

quiz.question: What does an array name represent?
quiz.explanation: The array name represents the address of the first element.

chapters.title: Dynamic Memory Allocation
chapters.description: Allocating and managing memory at runtime using pointers

pages.title: Introduction to Dynamic Memory Allocation
pages.content: Dynamic Memory Allocation (DMA) allows programs to allocate memory during runtime instead of compile time. It is useful when the amount of memory needed is not known in advance. In C, dynamic memory is allocated from the heap using functions provided in the stdlib.h library.
keyPoints: Memory must be freed after use

quiz.question: Which library provides dynamic memory allocation functions?
quiz.explanation: stdlib.h contains functions like malloc, calloc, realloc, and free.

pages.title: malloc() Function
pages.content: The malloc() function allocates a specified number of bytes in memory and returns a pointer to the allocated memory. The memory is not initialized and may contain garbage values.

quiz.question: Which function allocates memory without initialization?
quiz.explanation: malloc allocates memory but does not initialize it.

pages.title: calloc() Function
pages.content: The calloc() function allocates memory for multiple elements and initializes all bytes to zero. It requires two parameters: the number of elements and the size of each element.
keyPoints: calloc allocates memory for multiple elements
Safer than malloc in some cases

quiz.question: Which function initializes allocated memory to zero?
quiz.explanation: calloc initializes allocated memory with zero values.

pages.title: realloc() Function
pages.content: The realloc() function is used to resize previously allocated memory. It helps expand or shrink memory blocks without losing existing data.

quiz.question: Which function resizes previously allocated memory?
quiz.explanation: realloc resizes existing memory blocks.

pages.title: free() Function
pages.content: The free() function releases dynamically allocated memory back to the system. If memory is not freed properly, it may cause memory leaks.
keyPoints: Should be used after malloc or calloc

quiz.question: Which function releases dynamically allocated memory?
quiz.explanation: free releases allocated memory back to the system.

chapters.title: Structures
chapters.description: User-defined data types used to group different types of data together

pages.title: Introduction to Structures
pages.content: A structure in C is a user-defined data type that allows grouping variables of different data types under one name. Structures are useful when representing real-world entities such as students, employees, or products where multiple attributes need to be stored together.
keyPoints: Members can have different data types

quiz.question: Which keyword is used to define a structure?
quiz.explanation: The struct keyword is used to define a structure in C.

pages.title: Declaring and Initializing Structures
pages.content: After defining a structure, variables of that structure type can be declared. These variables can then be initialized with values for each member.
keyPoints: Structure variables are declared after structure definition
Members are accessed using dot operator

quiz.question: Which operator is used to access structure members?
quiz.explanation: The dot operator (.) is used to access structure members.

pages.title: Array of Structures
pages.content: An array of structures allows storing multiple records of the same structure type. It is useful when managing data for multiple entities such as students or employees.
keyPoints: Useful for storing collections of objects

quiz.question: What is used to store multiple structure records?
quiz.explanation: An array of structures stores multiple records.

pages.title: Pointers to Structures
pages.content: Structures can also be accessed using pointers. When a pointer is used to refer to a structure, the arrow operator (->) is used to access members.
keyPoints: Used in dynamic memory and linked lists

quiz.question: Which operator accesses members through a pointer?
quiz.explanation: The arrow operator (->) accesses structure members through pointers.

pages.content: Structures are commonly used in real-world applications such as storing student records. Below is a simple program that stores and displays student information.

quiz.question: Which concept groups different data types together?
quiz.explanation: Structures group different types of variables together.

chapters.title: Unions
chapters.description: Understanding unions and how they share memory among members

pages.title: Introduction to Unions
pages.content: A union in C is a user-defined data type similar to a structure. The key difference is that in a union all members share the same memory location. This means only one member can hold a value at a time. Unions are used when memory optimization is important.
keyPoints: All members share the same memory
Only one member can store value at a time

quiz.question: What is the main feature of a union?
quiz.explanation: All members of a union share the same memory location.

pages.title: Declaring and Using Unions
pages.content: Unions are declared using the union keyword. After defining a union, variables of that union type can be declared and used similarly to structures.
keyPoints: Union variables are created after definition

quiz.question: Which keyword is used to define a union?
quiz.explanation: The union keyword defines a union in C.

pages.title: Union Memory Behavior
pages.content: Since all union members share the same memory, assigning a value to one member overwrites the value stored by another member. This behavior is different from structures where each member has separate memory.
keyPoints: Only one member stores valid value at a time

quiz.question: What happens when another member of a union is assigned a value?
quiz.explanation: Assigning a value to another union member overwrites the previous value.

pages.title: Difference Between Structure and Union
pages.content: Structures allocate separate memory for each member, while unions share a single memory location among all members. Structures allow storing multiple values simultaneously, while unions allow storing only one value at a time.
keyPoints: Union size equals largest member size

quiz.question: Which data type shares memory between members?
quiz.explanation: Union members share the same memory location.

pages.title: Union Program Example
pages.content: Unions are often used when a variable may store different types of data but only one at a time. This helps reduce memory usage in systems where memory is limited.
keyPoints: Used when memory optimization is required
Only one member should be used at a time

quiz.question: Where are unions commonly used?
quiz.explanation: Unions help optimize memory usage.

chapters.title: File Handling
chapters.description: Working with files to store and retrieve data in C

pages.title: Introduction to File Handling
pages.content: File handling in C allows programs to store data permanently in files instead of temporary memory. Files help save information that can be accessed later even after the program stops running. In C, file operations are performed using the FILE pointer and functions available in the stdio.h library.
keyPoints: FILE pointer is used to handle files
File functions are available in stdio.h
Files must be closed after use

quiz.question: Which pointer type is used for file handling?
quiz.explanation: FILE* pointer is used for file operations in C.

pages.title: Opening and Closing Files
pages.content: Files are opened using the fopen() function. It requires the filename and mode as parameters. After finishing file operations, the file should be closed using fclose() to free resources.

quiz.question: Which function closes a file?
quiz.explanation: fclose() closes an open file.

pages.title: Writing to Files
pages.content: Data can be written to a file using functions like fprintf(), fputs(), and fputc(). These functions allow writing formatted text or characters into a file.

quiz.question: Which function writes formatted data to a file?
quiz.explanation: fprintf() writes formatted data into files.

pages.title: Reading from Files
pages.content: Data can be read from files using functions such as fscanf(), fgets(), and fgetc(). These functions help retrieve data stored in files.

quiz.question: Which function reads formatted data from a file?
quiz.explanation: fscanf() reads formatted data from files.

pages.title: File Program Example
pages.content: Below is a simple example that writes data into a file and then reads the data from the same file.
keyPoints: Programs can both read and write files
Useful for logs, reports, and data storage

quiz.question: Which mode is used to write data to a file?
quiz.explanation: w mode opens a file for writing.

pages.title: Introduction to Preprocessor
pages.content: The C preprocessor is a tool that processes source code before compilation. Preprocessor directives begin with the '#' symbol and instruct the compiler to perform certain actions such as including files, defining constants, or controlling compilation.
keyPoints: Used for macros and file inclusion

quiz.question: Which symbol begins a preprocessor directive?
quiz.explanation: All preprocessor directives begin with the # symbol.

pages.title: #include Directive
pages.content: The #include directive is used to include header files in a program. Header files contain declarations for library functions such as printf() and scanf().
keyPoints: Used at the top of the program

quiz.question: Which directive includes header files?
quiz.explanation: #include is used to include header files.

pages.title: #define Macro
pages.content: The #define directive is used to define symbolic constants or macros. Macros help make programs easier to read and maintain.

quiz.question: Which directive defines symbolic constants?
quiz.explanation: #define creates symbolic constants.

pages.title: Conditional Compilation
pages.content: Conditional compilation allows certain parts of code to be compiled only if specific conditions are met. It uses directives such as #if, #ifdef, #ifndef, #else, and #endif.
keyPoints: Used for debugging and platform differences

quiz.question: Which directive checks if a macro is defined?
quiz.explanation: #ifdef checks whether a macro is defined.

pages.title: Macro Function Example
pages.content: Macros can also act like functions. These are called function-like macros and they expand during preprocessing.

quiz.question: What does the macro SQUARE(x) do?
quiz.explanation: SQUARE(x) multiplies x by itself.

chapters.title: Storage Classes
chapters.description: Understanding the scope, lifetime, and visibility of variables in C

pages.title: Introduction to Storage Classes
pages.content: Storage classes in C determine the lifetime, scope, and visibility of variables and functions. They define where variables are stored in memory and how long they exist during program execution. The main storage classes in C are auto, register, static, and extern.
keyPoints: Four main types: auto, register, static, extern

quiz.question: How many main storage classes exist in C?
quiz.explanation: C has four storage classes: auto, register, static, and extern.

pages.title: Auto Storage Class
pages.content: The auto storage class is the default storage class for local variables declared inside functions. These variables are automatically created when the function starts and destroyed when the function ends.

quiz.question: Which storage class is default for local variables?
quiz.explanation: auto is the default storage class for local variables.

pages.title: Register Storage Class
pages.content: The register storage class requests the compiler to store variables in CPU registers instead of memory for faster access. It is commonly used for frequently accessed variables such as loop counters.

quiz.question: Which storage class stores variables in CPU registers?
quiz.explanation: register variables are stored in CPU registers.

pages.title: Static Storage Class
pages.content: The static storage class allows a variable to retain its value between function calls. Static variables are initialized only once and their value persists throughout the program execution.

quiz.question: Which storage class retains value between function calls?
quiz.explanation: static variables keep their value between function calls.

pages.title: Extern Storage Class
pages.content: The extern storage class is used to declare global variables that are defined in another file or outside the current scope. It allows multiple source files to share the same variable.

quiz.question: Which storage class allows sharing variables across files?
quiz.explanation: extern allows variables to be accessed across multiple files.

interviewQuestions.question: What is C programming language?
interviewQuestions.answer: C is a general-purpose procedural programming language developed by Dennis Ritchie. It is widely used for system programming, embedded systems, and operating systems.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between C and C++?
interviewQuestions.answer: C is a procedural programming language while C++ supports object-oriented programming features such as classes, inheritance, and polymorphism.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a pointer in C?
interviewQuestions.answer: A pointer is a variable that stores the memory address of another variable.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between malloc() and calloc()?
interviewQuestions.answer: malloc() allocates memory but does not initialize it, whereas calloc() allocates memory and initializes all bytes to zero.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a structure in C?
interviewQuestions.answer: A structure is a user-defined data type that groups variables of different data types under one name.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between structure and union?
interviewQuestions.answer: In a structure, each member has its own memory location, while in a union all members share the same memory location.

interviewQuestions.question: What is recursion?
interviewQuestions.answer: Recursion is a technique where a function calls itself to solve a problem.

interviewQuestions.question: What is dynamic memory allocation?
interviewQuestions.answer: Dynamic memory allocation allows programs to allocate memory during runtime using functions such as malloc(), calloc(), realloc(), and free().

interviewQuestions.question: What is a null pointer?
interviewQuestions.answer: A null pointer is a pointer that does not point to any valid memory location. It is usually assigned the value NULL.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between call by value and call by reference?
interviewQuestions.answer: In call by value, a copy of the variable is passed to the function. In call by reference, the address of the variable is passed so the function can modify the original value.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the use of static keyword?
interviewQuestions.answer: The static keyword allows a variable to retain its value between function calls and limits its scope depending on where it is declared.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a segmentation fault?
interviewQuestions.answer: A segmentation fault occurs when a program tries to access memory that it is not allowed to access.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between array and pointer?
interviewQuestions.answer: An array is a collection of elements stored in contiguous memory, while a pointer is a variable that stores the address of another variable.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the use of sizeof operator?
interviewQuestions.answer: The sizeof operator returns the memory size of a variable or data type in bytes.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a memory leak?
interviewQuestions.answer: A memory leak occurs when dynamically allocated memory is not released using free(), causing memory to remain allocated unnecessarily.
